Title:
Read Deep, Write Shallow: How Looped Language Models Should Spend Their Depth

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
13 pages, 8 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/read-deep-write-shallow

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models reuse one block of layers several times per token and spend the same number of loops on the prompt (prefill) and on every generated token (decoding). We show that the two buy different things: prefill depth mainly buys knowledge and long-context accuracy, while decoding depth mainly buys multi-step reasoning. A small connector trained on a frozen looped model separates the two budgets: one set of parameters serves all 16 pairs of prefill and decoding depth up to four loops, and one stored prompt KV cache serves every decoding loop exactly. On Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, reading the prompt with four loops and writing with two scores above the native two-loop model on all eight standard benchmarks we test, at the same decoding depth, and within two points of the native four-loop model on six; on GSM8K it is 1.0 point below the four-loop model on the full test set and answers in 0.55x its time. The same split makes a looped decision model more accurate at one to three decision loops. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/read-deep-write-shallow
